notice: Synthetic acceptance-test scenarios. Report text is invented fixture data, not verified Lionance findings or public reviews.

campaign.title: [QA] Lionance first-use and recovery - no trades
campaign.description: A labelled acceptance test of the LionDApp testing workflow using Lionance. Free, two places, no SKR reward. Check first-use clarity and recovery without buying, selling or signing transactions. Positive and negative findings are equally valid. Please record your app version and actual observations; do not copy sample reports as real findings.
campaign.appVersion: 0.1.1 installed build; record your actual version
campaign.requirements: On Seeker: 1) Open Lionance and describe what the home screen tells you. 2) Check an empty or invalid amount and whether the message explains how to fix it. 3) Leave the app and return; report whether your draft remains. 4) Describe what you expect after losing connectivity, and distinguish tested results from untested expectations. Do not authorize a trade. Include app version, steps, expected versus actual result, and one concrete improvement in 100 or more non-space characters. Evidence is optional; exclude wallet balances, keys and personal messages. A report identifying a problem can pass; praise is not required.

reports.firstUse: Synthetic QA fixture, not a verified product finding. Seeker, Lionance 0.1.1. I opened the home screen without authorizing a transaction and checked the amount field. Expected: a new user can distinguish planning from execution. In this fixture the primary action is visible, but the next step is unclear. Suggested improvement: explain that a review comes before any wallet approval. I did not test a trade or make a return claim.
reports.incomplete: Synthetic QA fixture, not a verified product finding. On Seeker I opened Lionance 0.1.1 and inspected the first-use screen. The main action was easy to find and I would welcome a short explanation of the review step. I did not record the empty-amount or background-return result, so those required steps are still missing from this sample.
reports.corrected: Synthetic QA fixture, not a verified product finding. Seeker, Lionance 0.1.1. Step 1: open home; the planning action is visible. Step 2: use an empty amount; expected a clear correction message, while this fixture shows a generic invalid-input message. Step 3: background then return; in this fixture the entered amount remains. Network loss was not tested; I expect a retry that keeps the draft, but do not claim that happened. Improvement: explain the valid amount range. No trade was authorized.
reports.negative: Synthetic QA fixture, not a verified product finding. Seeker, Lionance 0.1.1. I opened home, tried an invalid amount, and returned after backgrounding. Expected a clear amount rule and preserved draft. In this fixture the error is vague and the draft disappears. I did not test network loss or trading. Improvement: retain the input and give an actionable error. These negative observations satisfy the requested steps; they are not a reason to demand a positive review.
reports.networkRecovery: Synthetic QA fixture, not a verified product finding. On Seeker I entered a draft, switched away, and returned after a simulated timeout. Expected: one retry button and no duplicate submission. This fixture keeps the report but the loading state remains visible until retry. Improvement: show a bounded timeout, preserve my text, and explain whether the report reached the server. No funds were moved.
reports.longEnglish: Synthetic QA fixture, not a verified product finding. A first-time Seeker user opens Lionance and does not know whether selecting an asset immediately authorizes a transaction. The sample test checks labels, amount validation, background return and an untested network expectation. Expected: the action hierarchy clearly separates plan, review and wallet approval. Actual in this fixture: the review step is visible, while the recovery instruction needs more detail. Suggest an explicit retry message that states whether a previous attempt was sent. No trade, token purchase, profit expectation or wallet account change is included. This longer English report is used to verify wrapping, scrolling, expansion, review context and retained text after a failed submission. It is deliberately longer than a normal short comment and must not be truncated into a misleading success claim. The tester should be able to reread the published criteria before submitting, and the reviewer should see the full report before making a decision.

review.correction: Please add the empty or invalid amount result and the background-return result required by steps 2 and 3. State expected versus actual behavior; mark network behavior as untested if you did not test it. A positive review is not required.
review.unfairRejection: This sample rejection incorrectly demands praise instead of assessing the published criteria. Used only to exercise the appeal path.
review.appeal: The report includes the app version, steps, expected and actual amount behavior, background-return result and a concrete improvement. The criteria explicitly allow negative findings. Please review against those requirements rather than requiring praise.
review.resolution: The synthetic report meets the stated first-use, input-validation and background-return requirements and distinguishes untested network behavior. Negative feedback qualifies under the locked criteria. Approve the free result; no payment signature should be created.
